html:
The Chickasaw are a Native American people whose homeland lay in northern Mississippi, northwest Alabama, western Tennessee and southwest Kentucky. They speak a Muskogean language close to Choctaw, and their story tells of a migration from west of the Mississippi together with the Choctaw.

Hernando de Soto spent the winter of 1540 to 1541 in their country. When he demanded porters and women, the Chickasaw attacked his camp at night and burned it.

In the 1700s they were known as fierce fighters and close allies of the English traders of Carolina. They raided neighbours for captives to sell into the slave trade, and they beat off French armies from Louisiana in the Chickasaw Wars of 1736 and 1739 to 1740.

By the Treaty of Pontotoc in 1832 they sold their land to the United States, and in 1837 most moved to Indian Territory, at first among the Choctaw. Their removal was part of the Trail of Tears. The Chickasaw Nation, based in Oklahoma, is their government today.
